sections.title: Living Constitution
sections.html: This is a living, breathing constitution that will change and evolve over the lifetime of this league. Changes will happen between seasons as often as possible, and will be effective from that point moving forward. If you have suggestions for changes, please submit them to one of the executive committee members.

sections.title: LEAGUE FINANCING
sections.html: The league fee for O8FFL will be charged to each team owner and committee member, payable to the commissioner on or before draft day each year.
sections.text: The league fee for O8FFL will be charged to each team owner and committee member, payable to the commissioner on or before draft day each year.

sections.title: League Fee
sections.html: The O8FFL league participation fee for the 2025 season will be $150.00 from each owner. In 2025, league fees will be used for league overhead (ie draft board, trophy updates, etc) with the balance being used for prize money at the end of the season.
sections.text: The O8FFL league participation fee for the 2025 season will be $150.00 from each owner. In 2025, league fees will be used for league overhead (ie draft board, trophy updates, etc) with the balance being used for prize money at the end of the season.

sections.title: Late Payment
sections.html: If payment is not made on or before draft day, your team will be locked during the draft and you will be forced to auto-draft for that particular season.
sections.text: If payment is not made on or before draft day, your team will be locked during the draft and you will be forced to auto-draft for that particular season.

sections.title: Prize Money
sections.html:
League prize money will be paid out within seven days of the completion of the O8FFL Super Bowl.

  • Playoff Awards
    • Champion receives $1000
    • Runner-Up receives $350
    • The league has voted to change the name of the Trombley trophy to the Moules trophy. Moules™ has to provide $50 worth of food & drink to next year’s draft. The loser must also complete a beer mile on a track unless otherwise agreed to by majority vote. This beer mile must be completed within 35 minutes. If the beer mile is not completed by the day of the draft the other owner’s will autodraft for the Moules™ team. Starting in 2026, if the runner of the beer mile sets a new worst time, they must do a 5th beer shotgun. If the runner sets a new best time during the beer mile, all other owner’s must shotgun before their first round pick.
  • Regular Season Awards
    • “Practice Hero” winner receives $150
      • Given to the player who scored the most regular season points

sections.title: Anniversary Bowl
sections.html: Every 5 years there will be an anniversary bowl whereby the league dues will increase by 50% of the current dues. The start date of this will begin at a time agreed upon by the owners starting no earlier than 2024.
sections.text: Every 5 years there will be an anniversary bowl whereby the league dues will increase by 50% of the current dues. The start date of this will begin at a time agreed upon by the owners starting no earlier than 2024.

sections.title: LEAGUE SETUP AND COMPETITION
sections.html: The O8FFL will consist of 10 different teams that all reside in a single conference. Competition is head to head, and a winner will be determined based on total points scored by active players for the week.
sections.text: The O8FFL will consist of 10 different teams that all reside in a single conference. Competition is head to head, and a winner will be determined based on total points scored by active players for the week.

sections.title: Regular Season Schedule
sections.html: The schedule will be a 14 week regular season, with each team playing every other team at least once. The purpose of this is to ensure no team plays another team twice multiple seasons in a row.
sections.text: The schedule will be a 14 week regular season, with each team playing every other team at least once. The purpose of this is to ensure no team plays another team twice multiple seasons in a row.

sections.title: Regular Season Rankings
sections.html:
Regular season rankings will be determined by overall winning percentage. In the event of a tie, standings will be determined by:

  • Total Points Scored
  • Head to head record
  • Head to head points scored
sections.text: Regular season rankings will be determined by overall winning percentage. In the event of a tie, standings will be determined by: Total Points Scored Head to head record Head to head points scored

sections.title: Playoff Schedule
sections.html:
After the completion of the regular season, the top five teams in the league will make the playoffs. The 6th playoff spot will be determined by points for and not record.

  • In Round 1 (Week 15)
    • The top 2 regular season leaders will have a bye week
    • The number 6 seed will play the number 3 seed
    • The number 5 seed will play the number 4 seed
  • In Round 2 (Week 16)
    • The number 1 seed will play the winner of the number 5 vs 4 seed
    • The number 2 seed will play the winner of the number 6 vs 3 seed
    • The two losers from round 1 will play for 5th and 6th place
  • In Round 3 (Week 17)
    • The two winners of the round 2 games will play for the league championship
    • The two losers from round 2 will play for 3rd and 4th place

sections.title: Consolation Bracket
sections.html:
After the completion of the regular season, the bottom four teams in the league will play for the Moules.™ In Round 1 (Week 15)

  • The number 10 seed will play the number 7 seed
  • The number 9 seed will play the number 8 seed
  • In Round 2 (Week 16)
    • The winners of the round 1 games will play for 7th and 8th place
    • The losers of the round 1 games will play for 9th place and the Moules™ award

sections.title: ROSTERS AND LINEUPS
sections.html: Rosters in O8FFL consist of 17 active players from any NFL team. There are no position limits, and owners are free to have as many players from any position as they like. There are 9 players in a starting lineup; the other 8 slots will be used for bench players. The only time in which a league maximum 18th player can be added to an owner’s roster, is if an active player goes on the injured reserve (IR). There will be one 1 IR spot per team. In this case an owner will then be allowed to add an additional bench player until their player is removed from the injured reserve list. At this time, the owner must either drop the player coming off the injured reserve, or a different member of their team to get the roster size back down to 17 active players.

sections.title: Lineups
sections.html:
Starting lineups in O8FFL will consist as follows:

  • 1 quarterback
  • 2 running backs
  • 2 wide receivers
  • 1 tight end
  • 1 flex (running back, wide receiver, or tight end)
  • 1 place kicker
  • 1 defense / special teams

Owners must submit their starting lineup each week, even if the lineup does not change from the previous week. Players may be added or removed from the starting lineup up until the start of that individual player’s game.

Starting in 2026, kickers will be removed and an additional flex spot will be added.

sections.title: The Draft
sections.html:
The commissioner will designate a draft day each season. Owners are expected to attend the draft in person and must have all league fees paid before the draft. The draft will be conducted offline.

Draft order will be determined by a selection process. Your right to select your draft position will be based on the previous year’s Final Season Standings reflecting playoff results. For example, if you win the consolation bracket you can choose where you want to draft anywhere from 1-10. This will allow to adjust for teams that may have a first round keeper that would want a pick early in the second round. Draft order selection must be submitted to the Commissioner one week before keepers are selected. Selections will be made as follows:

First Choice Winner of the Consolation Bracket

Second Choice Runner up of the Consolation Bracket

Third Choice Winner of the Trombley Bowl

Fourth Choice The Trombley

Fifth Choice Fifth place team

Sixth Choice Sixth place team

Seventh Choice Third Place Team

Eight Choice Fourth Place Team

Ninth Choice Runner Up

Tenth Choice League Champion

The 3rd round game of the consolation ladder will have no bearing on draft order. Please reference section 6.1 for additional draft rules regarding keeping players’ year over year.

sections.title: Free Agency
sections.html: Free agency begins each season upon completion of the draft and is closed to all players upon completion of the playoffs. Unlike standard leagues, free agency is done on an auction basis, meaning the player who puts in the highest bid for one particular player, will be awarded that player. In the event that two owners put in the same bid on a particular player, the owner with the lower record will receive that player.

sections.title: Free Agency Timeline
sections.html:
Owners can acquire players off the waiver wire any day of the week; however, a bid must be placed in the system before 10:59am EST for an owner to acquire a player on the same day. Any bids placed after 11:00am EST will not go through until 11am the following day.

The waiver wire will be 11:00am EST on Wednesdays.

Each player is locked in their current position at the start of their team’s game that week, and the waiver wire does not reset until Wednesday morning at 11:00am EST. This means that a player who has a Thursday night game and is left on waivers, cannot be picked up until the first Wednesday after their game. Hence, Wednesday mornings before 10:59am EST are the time in which the most waiver wire bids are made and are done at a premium price.

sections.title: Trades
sections.html: Trading is allowed and encouraged in the O8FFL, and may be conducted between any owners. Trades may include multiple players from any position, draft picks, and waiver wire money. The trade deadline is the Thursday before Week 12 of the regular season; no trades can be made past this point until the offseason.

sections.title: Trade Veto
sections.html: The executive committee reserves the right to reverse any trade that they deem inconsistent with league competition and fair-play standards. This veto will only be invoked in extreme cases where two teams are suspected of collusion. The owners in question may offer reasons why the trade should be allowed, but the decision of the executive committee is final once it has been rendered. If the trade involves a committee member, they may offer reasons for the trade to be allowed, but will not have a say in the final committee decision.

sections.title: SCORING SYSTEM
sections.html: Scoring in O8FFL will be computed to two decimal places. This will allow points to be awarded or deducted for every positive or negative yard and will dramatically reduce the chance of a tie game. Players are awarded fantasy points for each week that they are included in the team's starting lineup. Players may only start at one position in any given week and will only be awarded points as described by their position distinction below. The league will operate on a half point PPR system.

sections.title: League Keepers
sections.html:
At the conclusion of the regular season each team is allowed to select up to 4 players to keep on their team for the following season. The following rules are in place for keeping a player:

  • The commissioner must be notified one week before the designated draft day what each owner’s keepers are going to be.
  • An individual player can be kept for up to 3 years in a row, with the only exception being that rookies can be kept for up to 5 years in a row.
  • In order to create player turnover, the year that a player is drafted is considered the first year of their contract. This means if you drafted someone in 2024, you will have them for the 2024, 2025 & 2026 season. They will automatically be put back into the draft for 2027. Unless that player was a rookie, in which case they can be kept through the 2028 season. The extended rookie keeper exception also applies to players picked up via free agency.
  • If you are going to keep a player, that player does not just automatically get placed on that owner’s team. In order to keep this player, the owner must take them in the following season draft 1 round higher than they were taken the year before. Therefore, if an owner chooses to keep a player that was drafted in the 4th round in 2024, they will be taken in the 3rd round in 2025. If you have 2 keepers in the same round they will be stacked one round higher than they would have been taken. For example if you had 2 players that would be kept in the 6th round they will be drafted one in the 5th, one in the 6th.
  • If an owner chooses to keep a player that was picked up from free agency during the course of the season, this player must be kept as a 6th round pick the first year, a 5th round pick the second year, and so on.
  • An exception to this rule is if you were to drop a drafted player or a keeper and pick them up on the waiver wire later in the season, the contract would stay with that player. For example, if you drafted someone in the 4th round, dropped them and re acquired them on the waiver wire, if you wanted to keep that player the following year it would cost a 3rd round pick, not a 6th.
  • If an owner chooses to keep a player that they traded for during the calendar season (or the offseason) their contract does not reset when they are placed on a new team. For example if Team A drafted a player in 2023, kept them for the 2024 season, and then traded them to Team B at the end of the 2024 season, Team B can only keep that player for the 2025 season before they have to go back in to the draft pool.
  • The Chuck Schefter Rule will be in effect for the 2021 season and beyond. If a team trades a pick, the team trading the pick can no longer stack players that would be kept in that round. The maximum a team can “stack back” is one round in any scenario. For example, if a team trades their first round pick they will only be able to keep one of their players drafted in the first or second round the following year, not both. Previously a team would be allowed to keep both players in the second and third rounds. Additionally, any owner that trades their first round pick and applies the stack-back rule the following year to keep a player in the second round that should have had a first round keeper cost will also be docked a 9th round pick. Starting in 2026, the 9th round pick provision will be scrapped and owners will not be allowed to keep a player drafted in the first round if they traded their first round pick. They will still be allowed to keep a player drafted in the second round in the second round due to the stack back rule.
  • Other examples are
    • If you own your first round pick and you have 2 players drafted in the first round and you plan to also keep a player drafted in the second round, you may only keep 2 of the 3 players, one in the first and one in the second.
    • If you have 3 players that would cost a first round pick but you traded your first round pick during the year, you may keep 1 player in the second round (see provision above for change in 2026)
    • If you have 2 players that would cost a first round pick and you trade away both your first and second round picks during the year, you may not keep either player
    • If you own your first round pick and you have 2 players drafted in the first round and you plan to also keep a player drafted in the third round, you may keep all 3 players in the first-third rounds as you would only be stacking a player back one round.
    • If you have 2 players that cost 5th round picks and you do not have a 5th round pick, there is no stacking back, standard stacking forward rules apply and you would keep these players in the 3rd and 4th round.
    • If you own all your picks, and you have a player drafted in the first, second, and third round, you may keep all 3 players 1-3 as normal.
  • Once a keeper is selected 1 week before the draft, the pick is spoken for and cannot be swapped for a pick. However, Keepers can be traded for other Keepers. If a pick is included as a sweetener that is ok however the player is locked into the spot where they were kept and will just be transferred to the receiving teams’ roster after the draft.

sections.title: Waiver Wire Dollars and Free Agency Costs
sections.html:
The league approved waiver wire dollar rollover. Any waiver wire money an owner has left will automatically be credited to their waiver wire budget in the following year.

Each owner will still receive their $100 waiver wire credit at the beginning of the season, but additional budget for any teams with rollover dollars will be tacked on. The only contingency here is that no player can have more than $150 waiver wire dollars in their budget at the start of any season.

Ending 2024 season waiver budgets were as follows:

The minimum cost to pick up a player is $1, meaning if you’ve already spent all your waiver wire money, you cannot pick up any additional players for the remainder of the season. Conducting trades with waiver wire money is allowed.

sections.title: Other Provisions
sections.html: Any other changes made by the NFL during the season will be voted upon by the owners on an ad hoc basis. If an owner wants to propose a rule, they must attend the pre draft rules meeting. Once a rule change has been voted on, it cannot be voted on again for 4 years and requires at least two owners to support the revote. If a rule change needs to be voted on in between the annual rules meeting it will require a minimum of 5 owners to support bringing the rule to a vote and an 8-2 majority to pass in season.

If an owner wants to propose a rule, they must attend the pre draft rules meeting. Once a rule change has been voted on, it cannot be voted on again for 4 years and requires at least two owners to support the revote. If a rule change needs to be voted on in between the annual rules meeting it will require a minimum of 5 owners to support bringing the rule to a vote and an 8-2 majority to pass in season.
